pr.title: Settle how find routes usage errors, starts the agent, and talks to it
pr.head: b77e9cb4892df933500b417056baa4e1fc43edba

summary: multipass is a password manager whose CLI keeps every login in one encrypted store. The websites plan, which is ready and not built yet, lets each entry list the websites it is used on, and adds multipass find <url>, which prints the names of the entries for a page. Like grep, find exits 0 on a match, 1 on no match, and 2 on any error.
The review of the previous websites pull request left four details an implementer would otherwise have to guess. This pull request settles each of them in the plan:

1. Usage errors before the command word. parse reads options before it reads the command word, so in multipass find --bogus https://github.com or multipass --bogus find … the error can come before main knows the command is find. parse now returns the command word with every usage error, and main gives status 2 when it is find.
  2. Starting the agent when nothing matches. run starts the session agent only when the command returns Ok. So find reports no match as a result, not an error, and a lookup that finds nothing still starts the session.
  3. The request and reply on the wire. The request is find <n> and the page address, like read. The agent checks the address itself, because any program running as you can send one, and closes the connection without a Touch ID sheet when the address is refused. The reply is ok <n> and lines of match <name> and related <website> <name>.
  4. The README's sheet sentences. The README says each sheet names one entry and the agent hands over only that entry. A find sheet names a host and its reply names several entries, so the plan's README row now rewords both.

No code changes, and the plan stays ready. A second commit took the three suggestions of the first review: the command-word scan skips an option's value, a non-UTF-8 argument to find exits 2 too, and a table lists the agent's other replies to a find request. New acceptance rows and one new agent test cover these points.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Session agent: multipass __agent, a background process that holds the vault key between commands and answers one request per Touch ID approval, in src/agent.rs.
  • Sheet: the Touch ID dialog macOS shows, reading "multipass is trying to …". Declining it ends the session.
  • Usage error: a command line parse refuses, such as an unknown option or a missing argument.
  • Related entry: an entry with a website under the page's root domain that does not match it, which find names on stderr as a hint.
  • Counted body: the agent's framing, a short line such as ok 42 followed by exactly that many bytes.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:

  • b77e9cb: changes requested, with one open finding. The new reply table's last row swallows the sentence saying the reply never carries a secret, so GitHub drops it from the rendered plan.

groups.title: The websites plan
groups.kicker: Details of find's exit statuses and session-agent protocol, settled in the plan
intro: All the changes are in § 2.2, which describes matching and how find runs, and in the § 2.5 table of changes by file, with new rows in § 4's acceptance criteria. Nothing here is built yet; the plan is what an implementer will follow.

The session agent speaks a small line protocol over a Unix socket. A request is one line of at most 64 bytes, sometimes followed by a counted body, and the agent answers each request only after one Touch ID approval. The new find request follows the shape read already uses.

checks.text: The plan's claims about today's code hold on main: parse runs its option loop before reading the command word, run starts the agent only after the command's arm returns without an error, and the agent drops the connection on a request body it cannot read. Checked by reading src/main.rs and src/agent.rs at the base.
The pull request's Testing commands pass at this head: project check prints Project plans are valid., git diff --check prints nothing, and the grep -c prints 8.

files.note: § 2.2 settles usage errors, starting the agent, and the wire form; § 2.5 and § 4 carry them into the file table and the tests.

checks.text: § 2.2: parse returns the command word with every usage error, taking the first positional argument and scanning the remaining arguments when the error comes first. The scan skips the value of an option that takes one, such as --store, and a non-UTF-8 argument, which main refuses before parse runs, exits 2 too when the scan finds find.

§ 2.2: on main, run starts the agent after the match on the command, and any ? in an arm skips it, so no match must be an Ok result for an empty find to start the session. An error, such as a refused address, starts no agent, as a get of a missing entry does today. Checked by reading run and Ctx::open_prompting.

§ 2.2: the reply cannot be misread. store::escape escapes newlines, so each record is one line, and a website holds no space, so related <website> <name> splits at the first space after the website even when the name has spaces. A refused address is decided before the approver is asked or the store is opened, so the refusal reveals nothing about the entries. Checked against store::escape, read_answer, and handle_one.

§ 2.2: each row of the reply table matches what Ctx::read_entry does with the same answer on main. denied fails with the request was not approved, unavailable and stale fall back to the passphrase prompt, and failed <n> returns the agent's error. Checked by reading fall_back, open_prompting, and read_answer.

The paragraph after the reply form continues on this table row, after the failed <n> row's closing |. GitHub reads it as a third cell in a two-column table and drops it, so the rendered plan loses the sentence saying the reply never carries a secret, username, notes, one-time password key, or history. Ending the row there and moving the text into a paragraph of its own fixes it.

§ 2.5: the README row now also rewords the staying-unlocked sentences that say each sheet names the entry and the agent hands over only that entry, matching what the AGENTS.md row already does for the session-agent rule.
§ 4: this row exercises the no-match agent start. The earlier declined-sheet row ends the session, so this row begins with no session.
§ 4: the agent test checks that a refused find address never reaches the approver, which would fail for an agent that trusts the client's normalization.
